analysis.title: This Is The Real Bubble
key_insights: The valuation premium of S&P 500 consumer staples to the SPX is at its highest level in more than 10 years.
Puro Saxena argues the bubble is in consumer staples, not technology, where the forward P/E is near its COVID crash low.
After similar staples rallies, relative returns over the following three months have typically been negative.
Short covering has driven a sharp unwind in hedge fund gross exposure, leaving hedge funds net long staples for the first time since October 2025 (GIR).
S&P 500 Staples beat S&P Tech by 33% over the last 30 days, the largest such move in about 25 years. The only comparable period was April 2000 through October 2001 (BTIG).
Staples have also outperformed consumer discretionary, as investors pay up for perceived safety.
Staples' credit spreads have compressed over the past years.
Staples' forward dividend yield relative to the 10-year Treasury yield is at the 1st percentile.

sector_views.rationale: Valuation premium to SPX is the highest in 10+ years, dividend yield relative to the 10-year is at the 1st percentile, and relative returns after similar rallies have typically been negative over three months. The report frames staples as the bubble but does not use an explicit rating.
Per Puro Saxena, forward P/E is near its COVID crash low, so the report does not see a bubble in tech. No explicit rating is given.

risk_factors: Defensive outperformance has historically been followed by negative relative returns for staples over the next three months.
Staples' valuation premium to the SPX is at a 10+ year high, and their dividend yield relative to the 10-year Treasury is at the 1st percentile.
vol_and_positioning: Hedge funds are net long staples for the first time since October 2025 after short covering drove a sharp unwind in gross exposure (GIR).
Staples outperformed tech by 33% in 30 days, the largest move in about 25 years (BTIG). The only similar period was April 2000 through October 2001.
Staples' forward dividend yield relative to the 10-year Treasury is at the 1st percentile.
